KTP Associate - AI Software Developer – 17133 

College/Department: College of Engineering, Design and Physical Sciences/Department of Computer Science – Brunel University of London (BUL) / Kinseed Limited 

Location: Boundary House, Cricket Field Road, Uxbridge, Middlesex, UB8 1QG 

Salary: Up to £45,000 per annum, dependent on experience

Hours: Full-time

Contract Type: Fixed term 24 months 

The Role 

This opportunity offers an AI and machine learning specialist the chance to develop intelligent digital health tools that help occupational health professionals identify workforce health risks earlier and improve care. The role combines practical software development with applied research and collaboration with occupational health specialists. 

Based primarily at Kinseed, you will develop predictive models and agentic AI workflows for its MediWork platform, designing and evaluating solutions for health surveillance triage, summarisation, workflow automation and practitioner-supervised decision support, with emphasis on explainability and cost-effectiveness. 

Collaborating with Kinseed engineers, occupational health practitioners and Brunel researchers, you will translate AI research into validated, scalable features using efficient language models, retrieval-augmented generation, model optimisation and robust validation, alongside project management and knowledge transfer. 

This 24-month Knowledge Transfer Partnership (KTP) between Brunel University London and Kinseed Limited offers professional development, advanced training and industry-academic collaboration. 

The Company

Kinseed Limited is a UK digital technology company supporting over 60 NHS organisations and occupational health providers. Its cloud-based MediWork platform supports referrals, case management, health surveillance and workforce health services. Kinseed aims to make occupational health more proactive and data-driven, offering the chance to develop impactful AI products alongside technical leaders and customers.

The University 

Brunel University London was established in 1966 and is a leading multidisciplinary research-intensive technology university delivering economic, social and cultural benefits. For more information, visit: https://www.brunel.ac.uk/about/our-history/home 

Led by Brunel’s Department of Computer Science, the KTP draws on expertise in artificial intelligence, machine learning and applied research to develop explainable, efficient and trustworthy AI for workforce health.

Academic supervision will be provided by Dr. David Bell and Dr. Weibo Liu.

The candidate

Applicants must hold an MSc in Computer Science or a related discipline, with a strong background in machine learning and software development. A PhD in AI or machine learning is advantageous.

Candidates need experience designing, coding, testing and evaluating machine learning workflows, strong Python and AI/ML library skills, familiarity with version control, and the ability to analyse data and produce clear technical documentation.

Experience in agentic or generative AI, small language models, retrieval-augmented generation, model optimisation or explainable AI is advantageous. Experience analysing health data is desirable.

The Associate must work effectively across university and industry teams, communicate clearly, manage multidisciplinary activities and deliver projects independently and systematically.

Benefits

The position offers these benefits:

A £4,000 personal development budget and access to Innovate UK sponsored KTP training courses, including management and leadership development.
10% of working time allocated to development activities throughout the project.
Access to BUL’s resources.
The potential for a permanent role with Kinseed after the project, helping develop and scale MediWork’s AI capabilities. This would depend on performance, business needs and career aspirations; a permanent position is not guaranteed.

Closing date for applications: 7 December 2026 

For further details, visit: https://careers.brunel.ac.uk

For technical issues, email: hrsystems@brunel.ac.uk 

Brunel University London has a strong commitment to equality, diversity and inclusion. Our aim is to promote and achieve a fully inclusive workforce to reflect our community.

 About the job: 

 This role sits within CyberUnite, a €4 million HEA-funded all-island collaboration led by Queen’s University Belfast and the University of Limerick, with partners including MTU, UCC and Gas Networks Ireland, to strengthen the resilience of critical infrastructure across Ireland and Northern Ireland.

 The post focuses on research into network security for critical infrastructure, such as gas, water, and electrical grids. This specifically concerns Cyber-Physical Systems and the complex integration of IT-OT environments, supporting CyberUnite’s mission to develop resilient and adaptive cybersecurity solutions for shared social and economic systems.

 The successful researcher will apply expertise in programmable networking, network traffic analysis, and machine-learning to investigate traffic profiling and monitoring and intrusion detection on encrypted traffic in a zero-trust, programmable network architecture.

 A major focus is designing and implementing in-network machine-learning-based intrusion detection mechanisms based on collection of network telemetry/observability data in the CPS testbed.

 The role involves close collaboration with networking researchers integrating the IDS with in-network access control and policy enforcement. The role also involves collaboration with AI researchers integrating the in-network IDS with endpoint AI detection and agentic response models.

 About the person: 

 We are seeking an ambitious and collaborative researcher to join CyberUnite. You will ideally have, or be close to completing, a PhD in computer science, mathematics, engineering, or a related physical sciences discipline. You will bring strong research experience in cyber security and programmable networking, supported by a publication record in respected journals and conferences. We are seeking candidates excited by the opportunity to work on network security challenges in complex critical infrastructure environments such as gas, water, and electrical grids. We are particularly interested in candidates with hands-on experience in network programming and network security systems design, along with solid software programming skills. Experience contributing to research that integrates machine learning methods with network security in the CPS domain will be highly valued.< /span>

 You will be an excellent communicator who can explain complex ideas clearly, work effectively within a large multidisciplinary team, and build strong relationships with industrial collaborators across the consortium.

 We are looking for someone who is organised, adaptable, and professional; able to balance competing priorities, demonstrate integrity, honesty and openness, and travel to meetings, partner visits, and conferences nationally and internationally when required.

 To be successful at shortlisting stage, please ensure you clearly evidence in your application how you meet the essential and, where applicable, desirable criteria listed in the Candidate Information document on our website.

 About the Role 

 We are seeking to appoint a Project Engineer to assist in the delivery of project milestones and associated scalable deliverables. You will join the team led by Dr Roger Woodman, Human Factors Research Lead ( https://warwick.ac.uk/fac/sci/wmg/research/research-areas/human-factors ), working closely with the Agritech Team ( https://warwick.ac.uk/fac/sci/wmg/for-industry/warwickagritech ).

 The Innovate UK-funded Agritech project aims to develop Machine Learning for Fault Detection and Predictive Maintenance in Dogtooth’s robotic harvesting systems. Using robot logs, performance data and service records, it will develop explainable AI models to detect faults, predict failures and support targeted maintenance. The project aims to reduce downtime, improve productivity and enable fleet-wide knowledge transfer, while supporting Dogtooth’s commercial scale-up through the SME and ASG teams.

 Research Fellow 

 You will research, develop and test AI models for smart automation systems and robotics, covering perception, decision-making, prediction and autonomous control. Working with human factors specialists, you will integrate explainability into machine learning architectures to ensure fault detection and maintenance alerts provide quantitative explanations for technicians and system operators.

 You will undertake independent and collaborative research, publish findings in peer-reviewed journals and contribute to research papers. You will also manage project-related administrative challenges, produce regular progress reports and ensure project objectives and deadlines are met.

 The role will involve deploying models for real-time, embedded and field-based applications in agricultural environments. This is an opportunity for someone with research experience at the intersection of AI, robotics and human factors.

 About You 

 Research Fellow 

 You should have a PhD-level qualification in Computer Science, Data Science, AI or a closely related discipline, supported by a strong mathematical foundation in linear algebra, optimisation and statistics. You will have a strong background in applied AI and machine learning, alongside a demonstrated understanding of Explainable AI (XAI) and human-in-the-loop methodologies.

 You will have effective verbal and written communication skills, enabling you to work with colleagues and external partners and contribute positively to team and School activities. Organised, self-motivated and technically adept, you will confidently use IT to prepare papers, presentations and technical documentation. You will demonstrate good time management, engage constructively with the wider academic community and adopt an inclusive and professional approach.

 Candidates who have not yet been awarded their PhD but are nearing submission or have recently submitted may be offered employment as a Research Assistant at level 5 of the University grade structure. Following successful award of the PhD and provision of evidence, they will be promoted to Research Fellow at the first point of level 6.

 Full details of the duties and selection criteria for this role can be found in the vacancy advert on the University of Warwick's jobs pages. You will be routed to this when you click on the ' Apply' button.

Job Description - Postdoctoral Research Associate in Organic Chemistry (26001468)
Job Description
 
Postdoctoral Research Associate in Organic Chemistry  (Job Number: 26001468)
Department of Chemistry
Grade 7: - £41,885 - £41,885
Fixed Term - Full Time
Contract Duration: 12 Months
Contracted Hours per Week: 35
Closing Date: 23-Nov-2026, 11:59:00 PM
Disclosure and Barring Service Requirement: Not Applicable.
 

Working at Durham University  

A globally outstanding centre of teaching and research excellence, a warm and friendly place to work, a unique and historic setting – Durham is a university like no other.

As one of the UK’s leading universities, Durham is an incredible place to define your career. The University is located within a beautiful historic city, home to a UNESCO World Heritage Site, and surrounded by stunning countryside. Our talented scholars and researchers from around the world are tackling global issues and making a difference to people's lives.  

We believe that inspiring our people to do outstanding things at Durham enables Durham people to do outstanding things in the world. Being a part of Durham is about more than just the success of the University: it is also about contributing to the success of the city, county and community.

Our University Strategy is built on three pillars of research, education and wider student experience, but also on our keen sense of community and of inspiring others to achieve their potential. 

Our Purpose and Values

We want our University to be a place where people can be free to be themselves, no matter what their identity or background. Together, we celebrate difference, value one another and are each responsible for creating an inclusive community that is respectful and fair for all.

Find out more about the benefits of working at the University and what it is like to live and work in the Durham area on our Why Join Us? - Information Page

The Role and Department

You will be working as a Postdoctoral Research Assistant (PDRA) in the Franchino group, within the Department of Chemistry at Durham University. The post is available in the first instance for 12 months, ideally starting in March 2027. Possible extension beyond the initial 12 months will be considered in December 2027. The salary is grade 7, spine point 32 (£41,885 per year before taxes).

Durham University, in the North of England, is a world top 100 university (QS World University Rankings 2026) with a global reputation for teaching and research. Durham University is one of the UK’s most historic universities, sitting in a beautiful, hilly city whose Romanesque Cathedral is recognised as a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Durham’s unique college system creates a strong sense of belonging, offers several social activities and provides students with additional pastoral care. As a PDRA in Durham, you will become part of a dynamic, friendly and international community, and benefit from cutting-edge facilities.

The Department of Chemistry is well equipped, with state-of-the-art instrumentation and facilities, and is located in the Science Campus, a 10-minute walk away from Durham old town. 96% of our research outputs were rated world-leading or internationally excellent in the latest UK-wide review (REF 2021). The Department and the Franchino group have close research links with industrial partners and other universities in the UK and abroad.

The Franchino laboratory has recently been completely refurbished. Alongside standard equipment for synthetic (in)organic chemistry, we have dedicated gloveboxes, an HPLC instrument, a microwave synthesizer, a mixer mill and a high-throughput experimentation setup hosted in a glovebox. Additionally, group members have access to departmental NMR, GCMS, LCMS, HRMS, XRD, elemental analysis and spectroscopic support units, mechanical, electrical and glassblowing workshops, and the University high-performance computer Hamilton.

The University provides a working and teaching environment that is inclusive and welcoming, where everyone is treated fairly with dignity and respect. We actively encourage applicants with diverse career paths and backgrounds, regardless of age, disability, ethnicity, gender, sexual orientation and religious beliefs. The Chemistry Department holds an Athena Swan Silver Award. The Franchino group is keen on increasing diversity, and actively seeks to attract and nurture the best and most motivated co-workers, regardless of their protected characteristics and country of origin. Applications from women and underrepresented groups are especially encouraged.

The Role

As a PDRA in the Franchino group, you will be pursuing ground-breaking research merging metal and organocatalysis, to develop new strategies for the selective synthesis of organic molecules. Your project is funded by a prestigious UKRI Future Leaders Fellowship (FLF, 1.7m € in total) recently awarded to the PI, entitled “ChloroCat: Unlocking metal-chloride bonds for data-driven stereoselective catalysis”. In this project, you will design, prepare and test organocatalysts capable of engaging with metal halide (pre)catalysts via non-covalent interactions, using an anion-binding approach. These binary catalytic systems will then be screened combinatorially, including with a high-throughput experimentation (HTE) setup, to achieve increased rate, unusual regio- and stereoselectivity and/or unprecedented levels of enantiocontrol. The mode of action of the binary catalytic systems will be investigated experimentally and explored computationally.

The project involves the following skills. It is expected that you are, at present, an expert on at least one of them, and looking forward to mastering them all during your stay in the group:

synthetic organic and organometallic chemistry (synthesis, purification and characterisation of substrates, products, ligands and catalysts using several techniques);

enantioselective catalysis (with transition metals or organocatalysts, and using HTE)

mechanistic elucidation using experimental and computational tools (e.g., kinetic studies, control experiments, DFT calculations and machine learning workflows).

The PI will share more details on the project at the interview stage, for shortlisted candidates only. 

Your key responsibilities are outlined below. You will cooperate will all group members, train younger students and behave as a positive role mode for the Franchino group, contributing to a supportive group culture rooted in research integrity, safety and passion for experimental research in organic chemistry. The PI will always be available to support you in your role, including providing technical expertise, advice on research and career matters, and help with international relocations. You will participate in weekly group meetings and problem sessions, and have the chance to attend group and departmental social activities. You will also benefit from our regular departmental seminar programme, and present your work at conferences, engaging with other scientists from academia and industry. Tailored mentoring and enthusiastic support to reach your career goals and improve your skill set will be provided by the PI, the whole Franchino group, the Department of Chemistry and the University (e.g., Durham Centre for Academic Development, Careers & Enterprise Hub).

Key responsibilities:

To conduct research projects under the direction of the Principal Investigator (PI), working safely and productively both on your own and in collaboration with others, as appropriate..
To plan and manage your own research activity safely, effectively and with minimal input from the PI, share research resources in collaboration with others and contribute to the ideation and planning of research projects.
To deal with problems that may affect the achievement of research objectives and deadlines by discussing with the PI and offering creative or innovative solutions.
To work with the PI and other colleagues in the research group, as appropriate, to identify areas for research, develop new research methods and ideas, and extend the research portfolio.
To assist with the development of research projects and proposals.
To understand and convey material of a specialist or highly technical nature through written presentations and oral discussions.
To prepare and deliver presentations on research outputs/activities to audiences which may include: research sponsors, academic and non-academic audiences.
To prepare high-quality outputs, including repots for the PI, papers for submission to peer reviewed journals and abstracts for presentation at conferences and workshops under the direction of the PI.
To participate regularly to research group meetings and engage consistently in problem sessions, striving to improve your knowledge as well as transmitting it to others.
To liaise departmental and university support units as appropriate for the progression of the research projects, follow all rules and guidelines in place in the group, Department and University, and make all required internal and external contacts to develop knowledge and understanding to form relationships for future research collaboration.
To be involved in student supervision in the context of the research group. 
To deliver training in research techniques/approaches to peers, visitors and students as appropriate.
To engage in continuing professional development by attending relevant training and development courses.   
To contribute to fostering a collegial, supportive and respectful working environment which is inclusive and welcoming and where everyone is treated fairly with dignity and respect, in the group, in the Department and in the University.
To engage in wider citizenship to support the department and wider discipline.

 

This post is fixed term for 1 year, with the possibility for an extension to be evaluated in December 2027 subject to availability of funding. 

You will be employed to work on research that will be led by the Principal Investigator (PI). Whilst this means that the you will not be carrying out independent research in your own right, the expectation is that you will contribute to the advancement of the project, through the development of your own research ideas/adaptation and development of research protocols.

You will, ideally, be in post by March 2027.

SECONDMENT 

The post is fixed term for a 12 month period and may be offered on an internal secondment basis subject to the agreement of the current line manager.

Working at Durham 

A competitive salary is only one part of the many fantastic benefits you will receive if you join the University. You will also receive access to the following fantastic benefits:

You’ll receive 30 days annual leave per year in addition to 8 public holidays and 4 customary days per year – a total of 42 days per year. 

We offer a generous pension scheme. As a new member of staff you will be automatically enrolled into the University Superannuation Scheme (USS).

No matter how you travel to work, we have you covered.  We have ample parking across campus, a cycle to work scheme which helps you to buy a bike and discount with local bus and train companies. You can also take advantage of our cost-effective and environmentally friendly Tusker Car Benefit Scheme, allowing you to lease a brand-new electric or hybrid vehicle with savings on tax and National Insurance.

We have a genuine commitment to developing our colleagues professionally and personally.  There is a comprehensive range of development courses, apprenticeships and access to qualifications and routes to develop your career in the University.  All staff have dedicated annual time to concentrate on their personal development opportunities.

We provide wide-ranging health and wellbeing support including discounted membership for our state-of-the-art sport and gym facilities and access to a 24-7 Employee Assistance Programme.

Our on-site nursery is rated Outstanding by Ofsted, and you can access holiday camps for children aged 5-16.

Our family-friendly policies, including maternity and adoption leave, are among the most generous in the higher education sector (and likely above and beyond many employers).

We offer all staff the opportunity to take part in volunteering activities to make a difference in the local community.

You can access exclusive discounts via our benefits portal including money off at supermarkets, high street retailers, IT products such as Apple, eating out and days out at various attractions.

Various salary sacrifice schemes are also available to help you take advantage of tax savings on benefits.

If you are moving to Durham, you may be eligible for help with removal costs, and we have a dedicated team who can help you with the practicalities such as house hunting and schools.  If you need a visa, we cover most visa costs and offer an interest-free loan scheme to pay for dependant visas.

Discover more about our total rewards and benefits package here.

Durham University is committed to equality, diversity and inclusion

Equality, diversity, and inclusion (EDI) are a key component of the University’s Strategy and a central part of everything we do.  We also live by our Purpose and Values and our Staff Code of Conduct.  At Durham we actively work towards providing an environment where our staff and students can study, work and live in a community which is supportive and inclusive.

We welcome and encourage applications from those who are currently under-represented in our work force, including people with disabilities and from racially minoritised ethnic groups.

If you have taken a career break or periods of leave that may have impacted on the volume and recency of your research outputs and other activities, such as maternity, adoption or parental leave, you may wish to disclose this in your application. The selection committee will take this into account when evaluating your application.

The University has been awarded the Disability Confident Leader status. If you are a candidate with a disability, we are committed to ensuring fair treatment throughout the recruitment process. We will make adjustments to support the interview process wherever it is reasonable to do so and, where successful, reasonable adjustments will be made to support people within their role.  

Durham University is a UKVI sponsor. Applicants who require sponsorship to work in the UK should note that not all roles are eligible. Further information on visa requirements and eligibility can be found on the UKVI website.

Contact Information 

Department contact for academic-related enquiries 

Dr Allegra Franchino, Associate Professor, Department of Chemistry, allegra.franchino@durham.ac.uk

Detailed Description 

The Biomedical and Astronomical Signal Processing (
BASP
) laboratory at 
Heriot-Watt
 University Edinburgh is recruiting a
 
large multi-disciplinary team of postdoctoral researchers for the development of advanced computational imaging techniques and their cutting-edge applications in radio astronomy, space geodesy, and medical imaging. The start date is September 1 2027, or as soon as possible thereafter.

BASP’s ethos  is to develop cutting-edge research on all aspects of computational imaging, from theory and algorithms, to applications in astronomy and medicine.

Multiple positions are open in the context of the £4M research Fellowship TomoGrav awarded by the 
Royal Society
 to Professor 
Kazunori Akiyama
 in partnership with Professor 
Yves Wiaux
 (head of BASP).

TomoGrav ambitions leveraging cutting-edge AI to develop a computational imaging algorithm capable of an unprecedented regime of joint precision, robustness, efficiency, and scalability for image formation. The core application is dynamic black hole tomography with radio-interferometric telescope arrays such as the Event Horizon Telescope (
EHT
) and its proposed space-based Black Hole Explorer (
BHEX
) extension. The algorithm will be transferred to extreme-scale radio-interferometric imaging applications with 
SKA
, to space-geodetic imaging for Earth reference frame determination, and fast dynamic magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) in medicine.

TomoGrav is supported by 10 world-renowned partners from across the world, whose combined expertise is second to none: Prof. Markoff (University of Cambridge), Dr Younsi (University College London), Prof. De Laurentis (University of Naples Federico II), and Dr Johnson (Center for Astrophysics | Harvard & Smithsonian) bring unique expertise in black hole science; Prof. Pesquet (Université Paris-Saclay), Prof. Schönlieb (University of Cambridge), and Prof. Steidl (Technische Universität Berlin) are leading experts at the interface of machine learning and imaging science; Dr Breen (SKA Observatory), Dr Elosegui (MIT Haystack Observatory), and Dr van Heeswijk (Lausanne University Hospital) will support TomoGrav’s planned technology transfers to, respectively, SKA, space geodesy, and MRI. The partners will actively participate to the research and host the postdoctoral researchers for secondments.

The TomoGrav award was recently covered by global media, see e.g. the 
Royal Society press release,
 the 
Heriot-Watt press release
, the 
EHT blog
, and our 
London evening Standard Interview
.

Key Duties and Responsibilities 

The postholders will develop cutting-edge research in computational imaging, each focussing on one or multiple facets of the project, ranging from the development of high-dimensional data models, imaging algorithms, and high-performance software, to their validation in simulation and their extensive use for impactful case studies across the range of TomoGrav’s astronomical and medical imaging applications.

Appointments are initially for 1 year, and renewable for up to 3 years, depending on research progress. The researchers will be encouraged and supported to transition to fellowship positions funded by any of the UK schemes by the end of their third year, aiming to both support progression towards independence and grow the TomoGrav team.

Education, Qualifications and Experience 

We are looking for outstanding candidates with a PhD in astronomy, physics, electrical engineering, applied mathematics, computer science, or a related discipline.

The candidates will have expertise in computational imaging or in one of Tomograv’s application: radio interferometry, black hole physics and astrophysics, space geodesy, or MRI.

hold a PhD (or be about to);

expertise in computational imaging, radio interferometry, black hole physics; and astrophysics, space geodesy, or MRI;

capability to be self-directed and think innovatively;

About the role

Bournemouth University is seeking a Postdoctoral Research Fellow to contribute to SCIFER (SIEM Solutions for Critical Infrastructures sEcurity & Resilience), an EU-funded project supported by the European Cybersecurity Competence Centre and coordinated by CERTH, with BU as the project’s Technical and Innovation Manager. The project is developing a federated, AI-native Security Information and Event Management (SIEM) ecosystem and an AI-enabled Digital Forensic Readiness Framework for critical infrastructures, with pilots in sectors including energy, rail, telecommunications and healthcare. 

You will plan, design and conduct technical research in AI-enabled security operations and digital forensic readiness. Your work will explore how artificial intelligence can strengthen the detection, correlation and sharing of security events across federated SIEM deployments, and how critical infrastructure operators can identify, collect and preserve digital evidence so that it remains forensically sound and legally usable, without disrupting essential services. You will contribute to the definition of use cases, requirements and the system architecture, support the integration and validation of project technologies in the pilots, and produce peer-reviewed publications, project deliverables and reports. 

Working closely with the Principal Investigator and with technical and end-user partners across the consortium, you will help shape BU’s technical contribution to the project, contribute to technical planning, integration and evaluation activities, including socio-technical testing with security operations and incident response teams, and support the exploitation and sustainability of the project’s technical outputs. 

You will hold a PhD in computer science, cybersecurity, artificial intelligence or a closely related discipline by the start date. Essential experience includes research in security operations, SIEM, digital forensics or AI applied to cybersecurity, practical experience of designing and running technical experiments, and a sound understanding of networks, systems and security tools. You will bring evidence of peer-reviewed publications, strong programming skills, and a commitment to research ethics and the responsible handling of security-sensitive information. Strong analytical skills and the ability to work independently and collaboratively are essential. Knowledge of digital forensic readiness, evidence handling, or the security of critical infrastructure and operational technology would be an advantage. 

This position does not meet the eligibility requirements for sponsorship under the Skilled Worker Route within the UK Visa and Immigration service’sPoints Based System.  Therefore, BU will not be able to sponsor individuals who require permission to work to carry out this position. The Centre’s emphasis on both technological and human aspects of cyber resilience provides a particularly strong setting for SCIFER, which brings together AI-enabled security monitoring, digital forensics and human-in-the-loop evaluation for critical infrastructures. You will join the BU research team that also delivers MosAIcSOC, a sister EU project on AI-empowered Security Operations Centres, with opportunities to collaborate across both projects. The Centre’s links with external and industry partners provide opportunities to inform the research through operational cybersecurity challenges and contribute to practical approaches for more resilient critical infrastructure defence.

At Bournemouth University, our motto is Discere Mutari Est - To learn is to change.  Guided by our BU2035 strategy, we are building a future-focused university that empowers people to thrive, embraces innovation, and creates lasting impact through education, research and partnerships.

About the role

Bournemouth University is seeking a Postdoctoral Research Fellow to contribute to MosAIcSOC, a €5.9 million EU-funded project coordinated by BU with 18 partners across Europe. The project is developing a modular, AI-powered Security Operations Centre framework, with applications in critical sectors including healthcare and assisted living.

 

You will plan, design and conduct technical research in AI-empowered security operations and cyber resilience. Your work will explore how artificial intelligence can strengthen the detection of, response to and recovery from cyber incidents, and how security capabilities can be tested and validated safely in simulated environments, such as digital twins and cyber ranges, before use in real-world settings. You will contribute technical expertise to the deployment and evaluation of project technologies in pilot settings, and produce peer-reviewed publications, project deliverables and reports. 

Working closely with the Principal Investigator and with technical and end-user partners across the consortium, you will help shape BU’s technical contribution to the project, contribute to technical planning, integration and evaluation activities, and support the sharing, exploitation and sustainability of the project’s technical outputs. 

You will hold a PhD in computer science, cybersecurity, artificial intelligence or a closely related discipline by the start date. Essential experience includes research in security operations, cyber resilience or AI applied to cybersecurity, practical experience of designing and running technical experiments, and a sound understanding of networks, systems and security tools. You will bring evidence of peer-reviewed publications, strong programming skills, and a commitment to research ethics and the responsible handling of security-sensitive information. Strong analytical skills and the ability to work independently and collaboratively are essential.

The Centre’s emphasis on both technological and human aspects of cyber resilience provides a particularly strong setting for MosAIcSOC, which sits at the intersection of cybersecurity, generative AI and human cognition. Its links with external and industry partners provide opportunities to inform the research through operational cybersecurity challenges and contribute to practical approaches for safer human-AI cyber defence.

About the role

Wild populations are facing increasing environmental pressures that can outpace their ability to adapt. We are seeking a quantitative researcher to investigate whether interventions could help populations adapt, and to understand their potential benefits and risks.

You will join Dr Katie Willis’s research group in the Department of Life Sciences at Imperial’s Silwood Park Campus to work as part of the MERGE (Modelling Evolutionary Resilience: from Genes to Ecosystems) project. MERGE is funded by the UK’s Advanced Research and Invention Agency (ARIA) through its Accelerated Adaptation programme, which explores whether adaptation in wild species can be accelerated responsibly to help address biodiversity loss.

Within MERGE, you will collaborate with researchers at Imperial, the University of Reading, the London School of Hygiene & Tropical Medicine and Topos Institute UK. You will also work with experimental teams across the wider ARIA programme, bringing modelling expertise to questions across different biological systems.

 

What you would be doing

You will develop and analyse models to investigate the potential benefits and risks of novel interventions intended to accelerate adaptation in wild populations. This will include investigating how genetic, demographic and ecological processes influence intervention outcomes and population persistence. Your work will draw on relevant literature and empirical evidence, alongside simulation studies, sensitivity analyses and uncertainty quantification.

You will work with ARIA’s experimental teams (Technical Area 1) to identify modelling questions and data needs. Your models will help inform experimental design, interpret findings and compare intervention options, connecting experimental evidence with predictions for natural populations.

There will also be scope to explore new intervention approaches within the group’s wider research programme. You will help develop existing proposals and contribute ideas of your own, with research priorities agreed with Dr Willis.

You will maintain well-documented code and analyses, contribute to publications, presentations and regular reports, and support relevant student research projects.

What we are looking for

You will hold, or be close to completing, a PhD in a relevant biological, mathematical or computational discipline. We welcome applicants from backgrounds including ecology, evolutionary biology, mathematical biology, applied mathematics and computer science.

You will bring:

Experience of developing and analysing mathematical or computational models to address biological questions.
Knowledge of at least one area relevant to population modelling, such as population genetics, population ecology, evolutionary biology or mathematical biology.
Scientific programming experience in Python, C++, Mathematica, R, Julia or a comparable language.
Strong quantitative and analytical skills, including the ability to evaluate model assumptions and results critically.
Clear communication skills, initiative and a willingness to contribute actively to the group’s research and collaborate across disciplines.

The opportunity to join an ambitious, fast-paced ARIA-funded programme exploring new approaches to help wild populations adapt to environmental change.
Collaboration with researchers across disciplines and partner institutions, with scope to help shape research questions and develop your ideas within agreed project priorities.
Access to Imperial’s dedicated career support for researchers and professional development opportunities.
Sector-leading salary and remuneration package (including 43 days off a year and generous pension schemes).

The post is available as soon as possible. This is a full-time appointment based at Silwood Park Campus, fixed-term until October 2028, with the possibility of a further two-year extension, subject to grant approval. Candidates who have not yet been officially awarded their PhD will be appointed as Research Assistant.

About the role

The Department of Infectious Disease Epidemiology within the School of Public Health at Imperial is a world-leading centre for research on infectious disease analysis and modelling. We have played a leading role in the global response to pandemics from influenza to COVID, mpox and EVD.

Can we detect pathogens in wastewater before they spread to cause a global pandemic? If you are interested in this question and have experience with PCR and sequencing of infectious diseases, you could be right for this role.

What you would be doing

You will be involved in the design and analysis of laboratory methods for targeted and semi-targeted sequencing of viruses in wastewater samples. This will involve both coding of novel bioinformatic methods and laboratory implementation of novel assays, potentially including the use of robotics and other approaches to enable multiplexed assays without loss of sensitivity.

What we are looking for

We are looking for someone with both coding and wet lab experience with a passion for genomic epidemiology, global health and biosecurity. You will be a team player but also self-motivated and able to deliver research and scientific papers on an accelerated schedule. You will be excited by global health research and the power of international partnership to deliver new findings and transform public health. A full person specification is given in the job description.

What we can offer you

An exciting opportunity to join a major international project delivering research on wastewater surveillance for pandemic prevention.
Exposure to international leaders in this field and opportunities for global collaboration.
Excellent laboratory infrastructure and a friendly research group with a diversity of talents and fantastic opportunities for collaboration across a range of disciplines.
Grow your career: gain access to Imperial’s sector-leading dedicated career support for researchers as well as opportunities for promotion and progression.
As a member of research staff you have 10 development days to use to develop your skills and explore your career prospects.
Sector-leading salary and remuneration package (including 43 days off a year and generous pension schemes).
Be part of a diverse, inclusive and collaborative work culture with various staff networks and resources to support your personal and professional wellbeing.

Further information

Please note that this is a PhD level role but candidates who have not yet been officially awarded will be appointed as a Research Assistant.

This role is for a full-time and fixed-term contract for until 31st August 2027 in the first instance.

If you require any further details about the role, please contact: Professor Nicholas Grassly at n.grassly@imperial.ac.uk.

About us

The Faculty:

The Faculty of Natural, Mathematical & Engineering Sciences (NMES) comprises Chemistry, Engineering, Informatics, Mathematics, and Physics – all departments highly rated in research activities and a wide-ranging portfolio of education programmes.

Celebrating diversity and supporting staff is important to us and we offer a range of provision including flexible working, caring support (including a  Parenting and Carers Fund and the  Carer’s Career Development Fund), training, and a variety of diversity and inclusion networks. Staff can apply for flexible working to help them balance the demands of their professional and personal commitments and we offer comprehensive leave policies for parental, adoption, surrogacy, dependant and shared leave.

The university is making investment in NMES and both student and staff numbers are growing. Our staff come from over 45 countries and 56% of our students are from outside the UK. Principally located on the Strand Campus in the heart of central London, further details available at  www.kcl.ac.uk/nms.

Physics:

The study of Physics at King's dates back to the foundation of the College in 1829. The Department is currently undergoing significant growth with substantial investment in new appointments, research infrastructure and laboratory space refurbishment. We offer a range of UG courses in both three-year (BSc) and 4-year (MSci) versions as well as MSc and PhD programmes.

Further information may be found at: http://www.kcl.ac.uk/physics  

About the role

We are seeking a highly motivated and experienced researcher with extensive experience in cellular biophysics, biochemistry or related disciplines that has experience in studying protein transport across molecular pores. 

The candidate should have deep understanding of protein nanomechanics, and possess orginal ideas of how the mechanical unfolding of proteins might be directly involved in nuclear and cellular mechanotransduction.

The project is funded by the Wellcome Trust. The project will be developed between the Department of Physics at King’s College London and the Francis crick Institute.

Within King’s, you will be part of the department of Physics, which belongs to the Faculty of Natural, Mathematical & Engineering Sciences (NMES). Supporting our staff is important to us and we offer a range of provision including flexible working, caring support, and training opportunities. The university is making significant investment in the Faculty and both student and staff numbers are growing. Our staff come from over 45 countries and around 56% of our students are from outside the UK.

Further details are available at www.kcl.ac.uk/nms

Further information may be found at:  http://www.kcl.ac.uk/physics 

Key responsibilities

Develop high quality research in the field of mechanobiology
Contribute to publications arising from this project
Contribute fully to developing and enhancing the research profile of the Department, Faculty, and University, including establishing a track record of high-quality publications
Use new research techniques and methods
Identify areas for research, develop new research methods and extend the research portfolio

This is a full-time post (35 hours per week), and you will be offered an a fixed term contract until 01/11/2027.

About you

To be successful in this role, we are looking for candidates to have the following skills and experience:

Essential criteria

1.       Demonstrate research experience in Biophysics, Biochemistry, or related disciplines.

2.       Extensive demonstrable experience with cell mechanics experiments

3.       Strong track record in the biophysics field according to experience

4.       Research experience, laboratory skills & ability to use/manage lab instrumentation.

5.       Experience with light microscopy and optogenetics experiments on different cellular organelles

6.       Experience in student supervision, grant writing and project design

Desirable criteria

1.       Experience with cell mechanics experiments

2.       Deep understanding of single molecule nanomechanical experiments

We are committed to working with our staff and unions on these and other issues, to continue to support our people and to develop a diverse and inclusive culture at King's.

As part of this commitment to equality, diversity and inclusion and through this appointment process, it is our aim to develop candidate pools that include applicants from all backgrounds and communities.

​​THIS VACANCY IS OPEN TO INTERNAL APPLICANTS ONLY​  
About us

King’s College London is an internationally renowned university delivering exceptional education and world-leading research. We are dedicated to driving positive and sustainable change in society and realising our vision of making the world a better place. We are delighted to announce exciting new opportunities to join our community.

EMBRACE is a visionary, multicomponent International research programme, the first of its kind in the world, supported by Inkfish over six years. It is a global study of 60,000 participants, including 20,000 mothers, 20,000 infants and up to 20,000 partners.  It brings together world-leading clinician scientists across six distinguished Healthcare organisations, world-leading AI & technology companies, together with premier biotech companies, with the overarching aim to fast-track major scientific breakthroughs, revolutionise maternal and early childhood health through precision-personalised interventions, powered by a groundbreaking symbiosis of cutting-edge AI combined with human support.

About the role

We are seeking to appoint two Research Assistants to join the EMBRACE Programme of research. As a Research Assistant, you will play a pivotal role in facilitating our research efforts to innovate and evaluate digital therapeutic interventions. Your contributions will support our research activities, spanning from participant recruitment to the management of different components of our projects. You will collaborate closely with a multidisciplinary team of researchers, clinicians, and research software engineers, ensuring the smooth progression of projects from inception to completion.

The post holder is expected to:

Assist in preparing and submitting ethics applications and ensure all research activities comply with university policies.
Conduct literature searches and evidence syntheses.
Support the planning and execution of research projects, including scheduling, resource allocation, and progress monitoring.
Participate in data collection processes and contribute to the analysis and interpretation of research data including related to use of a health app and smartwatch amongst others.
Analyse, interpret and write up results of your own research, contributing to progress report writing and publications.
Attend and contribute to team meetings and other relevant meetings.
Deal with problems which may affect the achievement of research objectives and deadlines.
Plan your own day-to-day research activity within the framework of the agreed programme.
Assist in the preparation of research findings for publication in peer-reviewed journals and presentations at national and international conferences.

The above list of responsibilities may not be exhaustive, and the post holder will be required to undertake such tasks and responsibilities as may reasonably be expected within the scope and grading of the post.

This is a full-time post (35 hours per week), and you will be offered an fixed term contract of 12 months.

About you

To be successful in this role, we are looking for candidates to have the following skills and experience:

Essential criteria

A Master’s degree in Public Health, Biostatistics, Digital Health or a closely related discipline, providing a strong foundational knowledge in relevant subject area.
Knowledge of digital health technologies and their application in health contexts, highlighting an understanding of the research area’s focus.
Strong organisational abilities, including the management of multiple tasks simultaneously, project scheduling, and resource allocation.
Demonstrated excellent written and verbal communication skills, including collaborating with colleagues, writing research findings, and presenting data.
Experience in preparing and submitting ethics applications, with a strong understanding of ethical standards in research.
Proficiency in participating in data collection processes and contributing to the analysis and interpretation of research data.
Ability to assist in the preparation of research findings for publication in peer-reviewed journals and for presentation at national and international conferences.
Capability to implement effective recruitment strategies to ensure diverse and representative sample sizes for research studies.

Desirable criteria

Demonstrate proficiency in data analysis software and tools to contribute to data analysis and interpretation tasks

Teaching Fellow in South Asian History

Are you passionate about helping to deliver an exceptional student experience in a top-ranked Russell Group University? Can you provide excellent teaching in BA History, BA International History and Politics and our postgraduate degrees?

The School of History is seeking to employ a dynamic individual who is passionate about inspiring and supporting our students with research-led teaching.

 We have an exciting opportunity for a postdoctoral researcher to investigate how phytoplankton physiology influences ocean carbon cycling. The successful candidate will join a UK-US research project, From Monod to Macromolecules: assessing nutrient-carbon coupling in a hierarchy of ocean-ecosystem models, based at the University of Southampton and working in collaboration with researchers at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology (MIT).

 The project will compare different approaches to representing phytoplankton physiology within the MITgcm-Darwin ocean ecosystem model. The successful candidate will implement and evaluate a range of physiological sub-models with the MIT virtual ocean environment, to investigate which aspects of cellular physiology are important for predicting nutrient cycling, primary production and carbon export.

 The work will involve developing and testing numerical models, running global ocean simulations and analysing model outputs alongside oceanographic observations. There will also be opportunities to investigate how the effects of physiological complexity depend on environmental variability and ecological interactions.

 We are looking for someone with strong quantitative and programming skills, and experience developing or analysing numerical models. A background in marine ecology, oceanography, biogeochemistry, applied mathematics or a related field would be beneficial. Experience with Fortran, high-performance computing and/or marine ecosystem models would be advantageous, but is not essential.

 At Southampton, you will work closely with Dr Ben Ward and Professor Mark Moore, in collaboration with Professor Mick Follows, Dr Stephanie Dutkiewicz and colleagues at MIT. You will also have opportunities to work with staff and students across the wider Marine Biogeochemistry research group and the School of Ocean and Earth Science at the University of Southampton. The successful candidate will be expected to contribute to the publication of research findings in peer-reviewed journals and to present their work at national and international scientific conferences.

 We welcome applications from all candidates with an interest in the role, and those who are committed to helping us create a diverse and inclusive work environment.

 We encourage applications from candidates from Black, Asian and Minority Ethnic communities, people who identify as LGBTQ+ and people with disabilities. We recognise that employees may wish to have working patterns that fit with their caring responsibilities or work-life balance.  Due consideration will be given to applicants who have had career breaks for reasons including maternity, paternity or adoption leave, disability or illness. We offer a generous holiday allowance and additional University closure days, subsidised health and fitness facilities and access to the Universities Superannuation Scheme (USS).

 Applications for Research Fellow positions will be considered from candidates who are working towards or nearing completion of a relevant PhD qualification.

 The position is full-time and fixed-term for 20 months, with an anticipated start in early 2027. 

 For informal enquiries, please contact Dr Ben Ward ( b.a.ward@soton.ac.uk ).
